QF.id: AIFM CII Legal Documents and Negotiations_29

question.text: 'Deccan Venture Fund III' has two founding partners: Mr. Vikram Bhat (IC Chair) and Ms. Radhika Iyer (CIO). LPs insist on a 'key-person' clause. What is the STANDARD effect of a key-person clause trigger in a Cat II AIF LPA/IMA?

answer.text: The AIF is automatically wound up and all unrealised investments are distributed in specie.
The manager's management fee is doubled to retain the remaining team.
The commitment (investment) period is automatically suspended until the key-person event is cured or LPs vote to continue, protecting LPs from deployment without the identified key personnel.
SEBI registration of the AIF is automatically cancelled.

explanation.text: The Logic: A "key-person" clause in a PE LPA / IMA protects LPs from blind-pool capital being deployed without the specific personnel on whose strength they committed. On a triggering event (death, permanent disability, breach of a dedication test, or ceasing to be actively involved), the commitment / investment period is typically SUSPENDED — new investments pause — until either the event is cured (e.g., a replacement is approved by the LP Advisory Committee) or the LPs vote to continue or terminate. Automatic wind-up, fee-doubling, and automatic SEBI cancellation are not standard outcomes. The Trap: Automatic wind-up is too drastic and economically destructive; fee doubling is not a recognised remedy; SEBI does not automatically cancel registration on a key-person event — it is a private contractual matter. Note: The XIX-D workbook supports identifying Key Persons/Executives, keyman insurance/indemnity, and notifying investors of situations that affect dedication to the fund. It does not specifically describe the auto-suspension of the commitment period as the standard remedy. Treat that mechanism as general PE-LPA practice applicable when reading AIF fund documents.
